sections.title: What you will learn to say

blocks.text: In this lesson you learn to say who has what and whose things are: «I have a brother», «this is my mug», «the helmet is mine», «the mug is my husband's», «whose keyboard is this?». English uses a few different words for this.

examples.translation: There is a brother in her family.
The mug belongs to my husband.
Who does the keyboard belong to?

blocks.text: To say something belongs to you, say I have: I have a key. Don't use there is for this — there is means something is in a place, not that it's yours.

examples.translation: There is a sister in our family.
Each of them has a wallet.

fixes.wrong: There is a key to me.

blocks.text: With he, she, it, or one person or thing, use has: she has, the hotel has. With everyone else, use have: I have, you have, we have, they have. It's the same pair as is and are.

examples.translation: A dog lives at the hotel.
There is paper on the desk.
The two twins share a dog.
A puppy belongs to my nephew.

sections.title: my, your, his, her — before the thing

blocks.text: my, your, his and her go before the thing and never change: my mug, my pencils — for one mug or many pencils. There is no mys.

examples.en: Your tissue is in my pocket.
examples.translation: I have the tissue that belongs to you.

examples.en: Her lunchbox is in the fridge.
examples.translation: The lunchbox that belongs to her.
The tattoo on him is small.

blocks.text: his is for a man, her is for a woman. Look at who owns the thing, not at the thing itself.

examples.translation: The tattoo belongs to a man.
The ponytail belongs to a woman.
The puppy belongs to a woman.
The bookcase belongs to a woman.

drill.question: You're talking about a girl's ponytail. Which is correct?
drill.explain: It belongs to a girl, so her.

blocks.text: our is for you and others, their is for other people. its is for a thing or an animal: its collar — the puppy's collar. its has no apostrophe. It's with an apostrophe means it is.

examples.en: Our printer is next to the window.

examples.translation: I can't find the laptop that belongs to me.

blocks.text: Test: can you say it is? Then write it's. If not, write its.

sections.title: mine, yours, hers — when the thing was already said

blocks.text: If the thing was already said, put mine at the end instead: The helmet is mine. Compare: my helmet, but The helmet is mine. After mine, don't repeat the thing.

drill.why: The thing was already said, so at the end it's yours.

blocks.text: To say a thing belongs to a person, add 's to the person: my husband's mug. First the person, then the thing. If the thing was already said, you can leave it out: The mug is my husband's.

examples.translation: The thermos belongs to my sister.
The piano that belongs to my aunt is old.

examples.en: The baby's bib is in my sister's bag.
examples.translation: The baby's bib is in the bag that belongs to my sister.

drill.prompt: Say the thermos belongs to your sister: «This is …»

blocks.text: To ask who something belongs to, start with Whose and put the thing right after it: Whose keyboard is this? For more than one thing, use are these: Whose gloves are these?

examples.translation: Who does the monitor over there belong to?

blocks.text: Who's and whose sound the same, but who's means who is. When you ask who something belongs to, always write whose.
People usually answer Whose…? briefly: It is hers. They are mine. It is my brother's. You don't repeat the thing — it's already in the question.

examples.en: Whose badge is this? It is mine.
Whose pendant is this? It is hers.
Whose binoculars are these? They are mine.
Is this pendant yours? No, it isn't mine.

blocks.text: my sister's bag — here 's means the bag belongs to her. But My cousin's here — here 's is short for is. Easy check: if a thing comes after 's, it means «belongs to». If a place or a description comes after it, it's is.

examples.translation: The flute that belongs to my friend is here.
The rabbit's bowl has nothing in it.

blocks.text: Before the thing: my, your, his, her, our, their. Without the thing, at the end: mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs. For a person: 's — my sister's.

drill.question: You point at a helmet and say it's yours. Which is correct?
drill.explain: At the end, without the thing — mine.

blocks.text: I have; he and she has. my helmet before the thing; the helmet is mine at the end. A person's thing: my sister's. Asking: Whose… is this? And its with no apostrophe for a thing.

examples.en: Her aunt is in the kitchen.
examples.translation: The aunt in her family is in the kitchen.
Who does the trophy belong to?
